explanation: Prospero's daughter Miranda, who has seen almost no other people, greets a group of strangers with 'O brave new world, that has such people in't'. Huxley borrowed it with heavy irony.

claims.text: The title Brave New World is taken from Miranda's line 'O brave new world' in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
The title's phrase is not taken from Hamlet, King Lear or Macbeth.
In The Tempest, Miranda says 'O brave new world, that has such people in't' on seeing a group of strangers.
Miranda has grown up on an island with her father and has seen very few other people.
Huxley used the phrase ironically for his dystopian World State.
